whatIsSection.title: What Are Corporate Tax and VAT in the UAE?
paragraphs: In the UAE, two tax provisions apply to businesses — Corporate Tax and Value Added Tax (VAT). Corporate Tax is set at 9% for companies with net profits above AED 375,000 annually. VAT is charged at 5% on most goods and services.

Both taxes are administered by the Federal Tax Authority (FTA). While the FTA manages both, they require separate registration, accurate filings, and proper record-keeping. Missing deadlines leads to penalties, so managing documentation carefully is critical.

items.q: Is Corporate Tax compulsory for businesses in Dubai?
items.a: Yes. Corporate Tax is mandatory for UAE businesses with annual net profits exceeding AED 375,000. All qualifying businesses must register with FTA and submit returns.

items.q: When does a business need to register for VAT in the UAE?
items.a: VAT registration is mandatory when taxable supplies exceed AED 375,000 per year. Voluntary registration is available above AED 187,500.

items.q: What documents do I need for Corporate Tax and VAT registration?
items.a: Trade license, MoA, passport copies, Emirates ID, financial statements, and bank details. We prepare and verify all documents for you.

items.q: Are Corporate Tax applicable to Free Zone companies?
items.a: Yes, but with conditions. Qualifying Free Zone entities may get 0% rate on qualifying income. Non-qualifying income is taxed at 9%.

items.q: What is the penalty for missing a VAT return deadline?
items.a: Penalties range from AED 500 to AED 1,000 per month for late filing, plus additional fines for repeated violations.

items.q: Can I claim VAT refunds in the UAE?
items.a: Yes. If your input VAT exceeds output VAT, you can claim refunds. We handle the entire refund process.

items.q: How does Setup Zone Dubai help during an FTA audit?
items.a: We prepare all documentation, coordinate with FTA officials, and represent you throughout the audit process.
